concerns.text: The plan explicitly states: 'Verified sources provide metadata only... The pipeline will execute using a synthetic dataset... for logic validation.' Using synthetic data to validate a biomarker discovery pipeline intended to answer 'Which gene-expression signatures... can reliably predict patient response' is a fundamental science failure. Synthetic data cannot validate the biological signal detection, cross-platform normalization (FR-014), or the predictive validity of the model on real biological variance. The research question is unanswerable by the proposed method.

The plan proposes approximating DESeq2 Wald tests using 'statsmodels' or 'pyglmnet' with 'synthetic counts (Poisson/NB distributed)'. DESeq2's power relies on specific mean-variance relationships in real count data. Approximating this on synthetic data does not validate the statistical rigor required for FR-005 (FDR < 0.05). The methodology fails to address how the pipeline will handle the specific noise structures of TCGA/GEO data, rendering the 'Statistical Rigor' claim (Constitution VII) unverified.

The plan acknowledges that verified URLs contain only metadata or single samples, yet the spec (FR-001, FR-002) requires downloading full RNA-seq count matrices and GEO microarray datasets. The proposed 'Option B' (synthetic data) bypasses the core requirement of cross-platform normalization (FR-014: ComBat-seq/quantile matching). Without real data from different platforms (RNA-seq vs. Microarray), the methodology cannot validate the generalizability claim (SC-003) or the cross-tumor integration (US-2).

The plan states: 'The plan will use rpy2 to invoke R functions... or fallback to Python equivalents'. However, the research.md admits the R environment is not verified and defaults to Python-native approximations. This creates a methodology gap: the spec mandates DESeq2 (FR-005), but the plan implements a statistical approximation on synthetic data. This approach cannot support the causal/associational claims about biomarker significance required by the spec.
